### TL;DR

Establishes a quantum information decoupling framework for infinite-dimensional systems, achieving optimal rates and enabling quantum-state merging beyond finite dimensions.

### Motivation

Existing decoupling formulations rely on finite-dimensional assumptions, limiting applicability to realistic infinite-dimensional systems like continuous-variable quantum optics.

### Method

Derives one-shot decoupling error bounds using sandwiched Rényi conditional entropies for finite-dimensional inputs, and constructs finite-rank projections on IID states to handle infinite-dimensional inputs while ensuring high success probability.

### Result

Achieves optimal asymptotic dimension rates for infinite-dimensional IID partial-trace decoupling, and extends quantum-state merging to infinite dimensions with the same rates as finite dimensions under finite entropy conditions.

### Conclusion

The operational interpretation of entropic quantities through achievable rates is a universal principle beyond finite dimensions, providing foundational tools for quantum information in arbitrary separable spaces.

### Motivation

### Method

### Result

### Conclusion

The aQPU framework offers a new perspective on quantum computation by integrating thermodynamics and information processing, highlighting the fundamental resource costs and paving the way for more efficient quantum computing architectures.

### TL;DR

This paper analyzes quantum correlations in a qubit-qubit-qutrit state from Higgs decay, mapping entanglement, Bell violations, and magic across phase space.

### Motivation

Understanding quantum correlations in high-energy particle decays can reveal fundamental aspects of quantum information in nature and test nonclassicality.

### Method

Using exact tree-level spin states and systematic expansions, the authors compute bipartite entanglement measures, genuine tripartite entanglement classification, Bell inequalities, and stabilizer Rényi entropy for the mixed-dimensional system.

### Result

### Conclusion

Higgs boson decay provides a rich platform for studying quantum correlations in mixed-dimensional systems, with potential applications to quantum information processing and tests of fundamental physics.

### TL;DR

This paper introduces a graph-theoretic framework for efficient detection of nonstabilizerness (magic) in quantum states using limited Pauli measurements.

### Motivation

Detecting nonstabilizerness is crucial for quantum computing but requires full tomography; the authors aim to reduce complexity by using a limited set of Pauli measurements.

### Method

They model simultaneous measurability via frustration graphs and show that when sign dependencies are absent and the graph is perfect, the reduced stabilizer polytope becomes efficiently solvable, yielding a closed-form bound based on the clique number.

### Result

The frustration graph structure determines tractability and provides a tradeoff between witness capacity and simultaneous measurability; Clifford covariance can enlarge detectable states without increasing capacity.

### Conclusion

Graph structure serves as both a certificate of tractability and a design principle for scalable magic resource detection.

*Keywords: nonstabilizerness, magic states, frustration graph, stabilizer polytope, Clifford covariance*

### TL;DR

This paper studies disjointness-preserving mappings on Calkin operator spaces affiliated with von Neumann algebras, proving a noncommutative Abramovich theorem and characterizing positive isometries.

### Motivation

To extend classical results on disjointness-preserving operators to the noncommutative setting of operator algebras and Calkin spaces.

### Method

Uses order-measure continuous mappings and properties of semifinite von Neumann algebras, with strict monotonicity conditions for isometries.

Shows that under atomless and finite conditions, any order-measure continuous disjointness-preserving mapping is zero; positive isometries preserve disjointness under strict monotone norm.

Provides a noncommutative generalization of Abramovich's theorem and unifies several prior results on disjointness-preserving operators.

Analytical derivations of moments and cumulative distribution functions for univariate and conditional CS-RBF densities, considering both untruncated and truncated support; mixture models with an incremental learning algorithm using k-means and stochastic gradient descent.

### TL;DR

### Motivation

The authors aim to characterize when sequences of Banach-decorated graphs have limiting densities representable by a Banach-valued graphon, extending classical graph limit theory.

They analyze homomorphism densities of decorated graphs and use functional analysis to relate representability to Banach-space structure, including separability, reflexivity, and weak sequential completeness.

For separable Banach spaces, uniform boundedness in every finite norm implies graphon representability iff the space is reflexive; for Banach lattices, it's equivalent to the Radon-Nikodým property; for dual spaces, it requires both properties.

### Motivation

### TL;DR

This paper studies algorithmic collusion in pricing, showing that collusion can be profitable while remaining undetectable by price-level audits.

### Motivation

Empirical work on algorithmic collusion typically tests whether prices are supracompetitive, but this paper demonstrates that such tests can be blind to collusion that preserves competitive marginal distributions.

### Method

The authors propose a collusion mechanism where bidding agents couple only through the joint distribution of unexplained bid components, leaving each agent's marginal bid distribution unchanged. They test this using language model agents and Ethereum block-building auction data.

### Result

The mechanism appears in real language-model agents, with residual correlation between deployments of the same model. The coupling decreases with higher sampling temperature. In Ethereum auction data, honest bidder pairs exhibit dependence that masks collusion.

### Conclusion

Since lawful multi-identity operation and conspiracy are behaviorally indistinguishable, the tractable regulatory target is not detection but counting of operators.

*Keywords: algorithmic collusion, price-level audits, competitive marginals, language model agents, Ethereum auctions*

This paper proposes a guard-agnostic defense amplifier for vision-language models against encoded jailbreak attacks, but it does not relate to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

### Motivation

Safety classifiers for vision-language models fail to detect harmful requests that are re-encoded into alternative forms like code or images, creating a 'decode gap' that needs to be addressed.

### Method

The authors build a recover-and-decode amplifier that transcribes image content and restates encoded text into plain language before the guard classifier, and evaluate it against an ensemble of eleven attacks.

### Result

The amplifier only partially closes the safety gap; the best guard-plus-amplifier still leaves 63-65% of behaviors broken, and no configuration achieves both low attack success and low over-refusal.

### TL;DR

InkShield is a proactive defense that protects handwriting images from unauthorized style mimicry by adding imperceptible perturbations to ink-stroke edges.

### Motivation

Handwriting style mimicry poses risks of document forgery and identity misuse, but existing protections for natural images are ineffective for sparse handwriting images.

### Method

The method selects a decoy writer to define a style-displacement direction, optimizes perturbations using a frozen handwriting-generation surrogate, and confines them to ink-stroke edges to avoid background artifacts.

### Result

On the IAM dataset, the Top-1/Top-5 retrieval rates of generated samples as the target writer drop from 11.94%/36.52% to 2.03%/8.79%, with minimal visual distortion (LPIPS 0.0078).

### Conclusion

InkShield provides practical, transferable protection against unauthorized handwriting style mimicry while preserving visual quality and readability.

Broadband metasurface focusing is limited by unit-cell phase dispersion and phase-amplitude coupling, degrading performance near band edges in conventional designs.

### Method

An artificial neural network models the unit-cell response in the complex domain to avoid phase-wrapping discontinuities, and particle swarm optimization globally optimizes a frequency-dependent aperture reference phase.

### Result

A metalens operating from 9.0 to 10.2 GHz achieves up to 4.36 dBi gain enhancement over conventional design, with peak gain of 23.8 dBi.
